question: The technique of classical dancing was codified by ______ in about the 5th century B.C.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The technique of classical dancing was codified by **Bharata** in about the 5th century B.C.
 
• Bharata is traditionally credited with authoring the **Natyashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.
 
• The **Natyashastra** is a comprehensive text that outlines the rules and principles for classical dance forms and has been influential in shaping Indian classical dance traditions.
 
• It covers various aspects of stagecraft, including makeup, costumes, acting, and directing, making it a seminal work in the field of performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharata Muni** is believed to have lived during the period between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• The **Natyashastra** is written in Sanskrit and consists of 36 chapters with a total of 6,000 verses.
 
• The treatise provides detailed guidelines for actors, dancers, and musicians, ensuring the preservation and propagation of classical arts.
 
• Classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and others have drawn heavily from the principles laid out in the **Natyashastra**.
 
• The work has played a crucial role in the cultural and artistic history of India, influencing not just dance but also other forms of art and literature.
